podcast.title: Dismissal from Suspect 208
podcast.body: A few months after the formation of Suspect 208, Noah Weiland was removed from the band for reportedly failing to attend rehearsals, a trait observed in his father. "A few months after they announced their formation, Noah Wyland was kicked out because, like his dad, apparently, he couldn't be bothered to show up for rehearsals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Son of Scott Weiland
podcast.body: Noah Weiland is the son of Scott Weiland and served as the vocalist for the band Suspect 208. "And finally, Noah Wyland, son of Scott on vocals."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Noah Weiland's Birth and Relapse (November 9, 2000)
xref.body: Scott Weiland's first son, Noah, was born on November 9, 2000. While Mary remained clean during her pregnancy and for 18 months postpartum, Scott relapsed shortly after Noah's birth, returning home from the hospital with a prescription for Vicodin after a dental appointment. "Scott was doing well too, but on the way home from the hospital where his wife had just given birth, he had a dental appointment, and he came home with a prescription for Vikiden."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Breakup
xref.body: After the departure of Noah Weiland and the arrangement with a new singer proved unsuccessful, Suspect 208 eventually broke up. "A new singer was found, but that arrangement did not last. And Suspect 208 broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Short-Lived Formation
xref.body: Suspect 208 struggled to maintain its lineup, with vocalist Noah Weiland being dismissed shortly after the band's formation due to reported issues with attending rehearsals. "Unfortunately, Suspect 208 just could not hold it together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
